en: The Apadāna of the Elder Avopupphiya Sakacintaniyavagga 2 I offered a single flower to the Buddha, the peerless one among men. Because of that root of merit, I have attained the state of an Arhat. Having abandoned birth and death, I have reached the end of existence. Through the power of that gift, I have attained the fruit of Arhatship. I am now free from all defilements; there will be no further rebirth for me. This is my final body; I shall not take up another form again. I have crossed over the ocean of saṃsāra, which is difficult to traverse. I have reached the further shore; I am now liberated from all suffering. I have attained the supreme, unsurpassed peace. I have realized the goal of the holy life, having lived it well. I have done what was to be done; there is nothing more to be done. I am cooled and extinguished; I have attained final Nibbāna. I have transcended all states of being; I have gone beyond all fear. I have reached the island of safety; I have crossed over the flood. I have attained the state of a sage; I have reached the state of a Buddha. “Having emerged from the monastery,
he stood up on the walking path,
proclaiming the Four Noble Truths.”
Teaching the deathless state,
having understood the word of Sikhi,
the best of Buddhas, the Tathāgata.
Having taken various flowers,
I scattered them into the air.
By that deed, O Lord of Bipeds,
O eldest of the world, bull among men;
I have reached the immovable state,
having abandoned victory and defeat.
In the thirty-first aeon from now,
because I offered that flower,
I have not known a state of misery.
This is the fruit of this flower-offering.
Twenty eons from now,
there will be a kshatriya named Sumedha;
Endowed with the seven treasures,
a wheel-turning monarch of great power;
the four analytical knowledges—
the Buddha’s teaching has been done.
Thus indeed did the Venerable Elder Avopupphiya speak these verses.
The legend of the Elder Avopupphiya is the second.
